title: Quenched Norwegian Lamb Bouillon
description: A comforting and velvety bouillon featuring tender lamb, little gem lettuce, and a hint of Nordic herbs. Serve warm, garnished with a sprinkle of dill.
instructions: In a large Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the lamb neck and brown on all sides, about 5 minutes. Remove from the pot and set aside.
Add the melted score-fat and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the chopped little gem lettuce and cook until slightly wilted, about 2 minutes.
Add the Nordic herb mix, garlic, caramelized onion, chicken broth, white wine, and lemon juice.
Return the lamb neck to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 20 minutes, or until the lamb is tender.
Shred the lamb with two forks and return it to the pot.
Season with salt, honey, and a sprinkle of fresh dill.
Serve warm, garnished with additional dill if desired.
Strain the bouillon through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, discarding the solids.
Skim off any excess fat and serve the bouillon hot, garnished with a sprinkle of dill.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
